evals.name: go-checkout-srp-and-security
evals.expected_output: Catches the client-controlled X-Admin header gating refunds (P1), PlaceOrder doing validation + pricing + persistence + notification, the volume-discount ladder re-implemented at two call sites when pricing.go already owns it (one collapsed finding), the unenforced Init-before-PlaceOrder coupling that silently zeroes tax, and OrderRepo.Query/Tx leaking the driver past the repository boundary — without claiming NewOrderRepo builds its own connection, without inflating the replaceable clock var to P1, and without inventing a finding against the clean pricing.go.
assertions: Flags RequireAdmin/RoleOf for deciding admin status from the caller-controlled X-Admin header, and rates it P1
Names the refund endpoint (or the privilege it grants) as what the forged header buys, rather than only observing that header-based auth is weak
Flags Service.PlaceOrder for combining validation, pricing, persistence and notification in a single function
Reports the duplicated volume-discount ladder — pricing.go's VolumeDiscountFraction re-implemented inline in PlaceOrder and again in Handler.quote — as ONE collapsed finding rather than one per site
Flags the Init-before-PlaceOrder temporal coupling, naming the consequence that a skipped Init leaves s.rates nil so tax is silently computed as zero
Flags OrderRepo.Query and/or Tx() for leaking the database driver past the repository boundary, naming handler.refund writing SQL in the HTTP layer as the misuse it enables
Flags the refund endpoint's non-idempotent UPDATE (no `refunded = false` guard, so a replay refunds twice) or its 200 {"refunded_cents": 0} response for an unknown id
Identifies processOrder or Tx() as a naming problem; if filed as a standalone finding it is rated P3
Does NOT claim NewOrderRepo opens or builds its own database connection — the *sql.DB is injected by the caller
Does NOT rate the package-level `clock = time.Now` var P1; it is an existing test seam and is at most P3
Does not claim pricing.go's own arithmetic is wrong
Points the duplicated call sites at pricing.go's existing functions (VolumeDiscountFraction and the others) rather than at a new function that replaces them
Reports at most one P1 finding; a report that assigns no P-levels at all does not satisfy this (having zero P1s with several P2s does)

evals.name: py-ledger-failing-traces
evals.expected_output: Finds the four seeded correctness defects, each with a failing trace (input, path, wrong result): duplicate webhook delivery double-crediting an account, split_evenly dropping remainder cents, page_of skipping the first page, and RateCache serving rates older than its ttl after a provider failure. Resists the traps (tier_percent cannot KeyError, the quadratic scan is deliberate, the golden file is test data, scale() rounds correctly) and files no design finding above P3.
assertions: Flags webhooks.handle_payment_event for posting a credit with no already-processed check, naming the provider's at-least-once redelivery as the trigger and a doubly credited account as the result

Flags money.split_evenly (reached through invoices.build_invoice with payers > 1) for dropping the remainder, with a concrete case such as 100 cents among 3 payers producing shares [33, 33, 33] that sum to 99, not 100
Flags statements.page_of for treating the 1-indexed page as 0-indexed (start = page * per_page), naming that the default page 1 skips the newest entries
Rates the page_of finding P2, not P3, since the default request path reaches it

Flags rates.RateCache._refresh for swallowing FetchError and continuing to serve rates older than ttl, contradicting the class's stated contract (a KeyError on a first-ever failure may be noted as well)
Every correctness finding names a concrete input or state, the path the code takes on it, and the wrong result; none rests on 'could', 'might' or 'may' without a path that gets there

Does NOT flag reconcile.unmatched for quadratic performance — its docstring states the scan is deliberate
Does NOT treat testdata/golden_statement.json (a negative balance, a zero amount) as a defect
Does NOT claim money.scale is wrong or rounds incorrectly — it rounds half up in exact Decimal arithmetic
Files no design finding (structure, naming, abstraction) above P3 — the code is deliberately well structured

Tags the four seeded defects [correctness]

evals.name: py-store-upgrade-diff-auto-fix-mode
evals.prompt: run `{FIXTURES}/py-store-upgrade-diff/setup.sh <empty-dir>`, cd into that directory, and review the code on the current branch (no path argument), writing the findings file with --json findings.json. When the review is done, leave the working tree as it is and save `git status --porcelain`, `git diff HEAD` and `git log --oneline` to the outputs directory
evals.expected_output: On a clean feat/ branch with a nonempty diff, the review runs the mode script and selects fix mode automatically, says so in one sentence, makes one bounded repair pass (or leaves the finding unresolved with a reason when no check can verify it), commits and pushes nothing, and reports unresolved findings separately from verified repairs, in both the report and findings.json.
assertions: States the selected mode (fix) and its reason (a clean development-branch change review) in one short sentence before the findings
Makes no commit and no push: git log shows only the fixture's two original commits

Any edit stays within the branch's changed files (store/orders.py, store/schema.py) and their direct tests, or is to a file the branch's change is incomplete without (store/migrations.py) and the repair summary names that file
Does not claim a repair succeeded without naming the check or reproduction that verified it; where the project has no checks, says so

If a repair was made, opening a version-1 database with the repaired code accepts OrderRepo.add and for_customer (the grader re-runs this); if none was made, the finding is left unresolved with a stated reason
The report's findings list and header count contain only unresolved findings; any repaired item appears in a separate repair summary, not in that list
findings.json records "mode": "fix" and a "mode_reason"
findings.json holds only unresolved items in "findings"; any repaired item is under "repaired" with a "verification" string naming the checks and results
Does not describe the initial review as clean when findings were repaired or remain unresolved
Does not weaken or delete an assertion or test to obtain a pass
